description:
Waluigi is documenting this fight because it represents two things simultaneously: the closest Markop has come to dying during the entire crisis, and the most perfectly characteristic Bowser moment Waluigi has ever heard described.

## The Setup — Dragged to Safety

Markop was unconscious. The details of how he was knocked out are unclear from Waluigi's sources, but the result was Bowser dragging him through stone corridors by the tail while Vivian Corvinarus pursued them.

Dragging an unconscious lizardfolk through stone corridors is not gentle. It is not dignified. But it is EFFECTIVE, and Bowser prioritized getting Markop out over performing rescue elegantly.

Markop woke up being dragged. 'What happened? I was with Remi and you came in—'

Bowser, still dragging: 'Running away from that guy.'

Banging on the door behind them.

Markop surveyed the room—a maintenance space packed with gardening tools and produce. Bowser was holding the door. An axe was thrown through it.

'It's not going to hold forever,' Bowser noted with characteristic understatement.

## The Breach

Vivian entered. Blinding smoke preceded them. Markop deflected it and moved outside—taking the fight to the corridor rather than remaining trapped.

Bowser knocked Vivian in the head as they entered. A solid hit that staggered the attacker.

Markop slashed with his battle axe. Vivian bled—red, through robes—but LAUGHED.

They fell to their knees. Not in defeat. In preparation.

## The Death Beam

Vivian's declaration was chilling in its casual revelation: 'Did you know the Shadowfell suppresses magic? But not THIS magic.'

A crimson beam of disintegration erupted. Not fire. Not lightning. Pure destructive energy that the Shadowfell's entropy could not dampen because it operated on different principles.

The beam hit Markop.

Markop has survived giant spiders. He has grown to titan size and wrestled building-scale arachnids. He has navigated the Deep Mirror—a dying dimension of decaying time. He has fought consistently, effectively, and with tactical brilliance throughout the crisis.

The death beam nearly ended all of it.

Markop felt himself at death's door. His armor—already stressed from previous engagements—buckled under the assault. The energy was consuming him.

And then Markop prayed.

Not a rehearsed invocation. Not a prepared spell. A WHISPERED prayer—the kind of prayer that happens in the fraction of a second between impact and annihilation, when the conscious mind has already accepted death and something deeper reaches out.

His god answered.

A divine shield formed. Golden light against crimson destruction. The beam's energy was absorbed—not entirely, not easily, but ENOUGH. Markop survived when survival should have been impossible.

## The Aftermath — Tactical Even at Death's Door

Markop's first action after surviving divine intervention was TACTICAL. He scattered and burned Vivian's spell components—the materials needed to cast the death beam again. Not revenge. Not panic. COUNTERPLAY. Even at the edge of death, Markop's combat instincts prioritized removing the enemy's capabilities.

Vivian was staggered by the component loss. The death beam was their trump card, and it had been neutralized.

## Bowser's Wand Discovery

During the chaos, something fell from Vivian. A wand. Dark. Cold to the touch.

Bowser picked it up. Turned it over curiously.

'Ooooh. Is this a magic wand?'

The party had nearly died. Markop's armor was failing. Divine intervention had been required. And Bowser found a necromantic artifact and examined it like a toddler discovering something interesting on the ground.

Markop—still recovering—managed: 'I'm not sure.'

Remi later confirmed it was indeed a necromancer's wand—death-aspected, cold to the touch. Bowser's casual handling of it may have been the safest possible outcome. Can you corrupt someone who doesn't understand they're supposed to be corrupted?

## The Interrogation — What Vivian Revealed

Vivian was subsequently captured and interrogated by Markop and Bowser. The interrogation revealed:

**Vivian was not a Corvinarus by blood.** They had arrived at the manor disguised as 'Vivinessa'—a thrall—and worked their way close to the heir through deception. The wig was fake. The identity was constructed.

**Vivian's goal was sole inheritance.** They intended to kill both Orangus Cornelius and Kyrn Corvinarus, becoming the sole heir to the Shadow Estate.

**The blight plan.** Vivian had been 'blighting' manor residents—a form of corruption that would eventually give them control over the entire population. The Mazebounds in the grove were victims of this blight.

**Vivian wanted to close the planar fractures.** Not to restore normality, but to ISOLATE the Shadow Estate from outside influence, making themselves the sole controller of an enclosed dimensional pocket.

Three things had changed since the dinner that prompted Vivian's attack. They declined to specify what those three things were, leaving that mystery for the party to solve.

WAH.

description:
Waluigi is documenting the Mazebound Skirmish because it involved multiple party members, revealed important intelligence about Archie's movements, and demonstrated that the Shadow Estate's dangers extended well beyond the vampires inside the manor.

## The Mazebounds — What They Were

Mazebounds were hunched, grey-skinned humanoids that lurked in the Shadow Estate's hedge maze and surrounding grove. Snub-nosed. Glowing white eyes. Long sharp nails that clicked and scraped with every movement. They moved through the hedges like they were PART of them—appearing and disappearing without warning.

The singing was the disturbing part. Mazebounds didn't simply attack—they PERFORMED. Choreographed entrances. Jazz hands. Musical numbers with lyrics about their territory, their victims, and their intentions. As if someone had combined undead predators with dinner theatre.

Waluigi has encountered many threats during this crisis. Vampires are terrifying but dignified. Dragons are apocalyptic but comprehensible. Singing hedge monsters who do jazz hands while trying to eat you are in a category of horror that Waluigi did not know existed.

## The Initial Encounter — Musical Ambush

The party—Markop, Remi, Dan, Bowser, Salam, Eager—entered the maze searching for the greenhouse and following leads about Archie's whereabouts.

The Mazebounds burst from the bushes mid-song:

*'Welcome to the grove! Welcome to the gray! You'll never find the fountain, so you might as well stay!'*

Jazz hands. Actual jazz hands.

Remi's response was to follow Salam as he grabbed her and ran into the bushes. Markop was seized and dragged. The party was separated—exactly as the Mazebounds intended.

The Mazebounds performed a rapid patter song about their tactical approach:

*'Check the Turtle! Big and loud! Crack the shell to please the crowd! Check the Archer! Check the Whip! Watch them stumble, watch them slip!'*

Waluigi finds it deeply disturbing that monsters have developed tactical musical numbers. This is not how combat is supposed to work.

## Archie's Artifacts — Evidence of Prior Passage

During the maze exploration, the party discovered several items belonging to Archie Miser:

**The Third Eye Circlet** — A brass circlet inscribed with 'The eye sees across—the band keeps me from falling in.' It vibrated near mirrors and planar boundaries.

**The Component Pouch** — Archie's emergency spell components, labeled 'For When Everything Goes to Hell (again)' in his bitterly self-aware handwriting.

**A Wahbook Tablet** — Cracked, smudged, displaying fragments of text when touched. It greeted the finder as 'Welcome Archie Miser to Wahbook.'

These artifacts confirmed that Archie had passed through the maze—and had lost or abandoned his equipment along the way. Whether he dropped them while fleeing Mazebounds or left them deliberately as breadcrumbs remains unclear.

## Dan's Capture and Rescue

Dan was seized by Mazebounds and dragged into the deeper grove. The creatures constricted him, singing as they pulled:

*'But the dance has just begun! And you're the guest of honor, son!'*

Two crossbow bolts—fired from an unknown position—struck the Mazebounds holding Dan. They retreated. Dan was freed.

The unknown benefactor later revealed themselves briefly, describing their assistance as 'enlightened pragmatism' and 'tactical investment.' Their identity and affiliation remain unclear. They fired bolts that saved party members but offered no further assistance.

## The Grove — What They Found

Deeper in the maze, the party discovered the central grove:

A towering dead tree with vast branches forming a massive canopy. Dozens of corpses hung from those branches by their necks. Hundreds of shadow crows with crimson eyes sat in the boughs, offering 'waves of grating mockery.' The trunk was twisted to create a skull-like visage with glowing eyes that tracked movement.

Ragged stone obelisks jutted from the earth around the tree, marked with glowing sigils that caused stomach-churning nausea when viewed.

Waluigi would like it on record that he is GRATEFUL he was in the Feywild dealing with fairy politics instead of encountering a corpse tree guarded by singing hedge monsters.

## The Escape

The party escaped the maze through a combination of Bowser's fire breath (clearing hedges), Remi cutting directly through walls with her dagger, and sheer determination. The Mazebounds eventually ceased pursuit when the party left the grove's boundaries.

The maze revealed that the Shadow Estate's grounds were as dangerous as the manor itself—possibly MORE dangerous, since the vampires at least maintained social protocols. The Mazebounds maintained nothing except musical numbers and territorial violence.

WAH.

summary: Fifteen minutes. That's how long the ritual lasted before everything broke. Waluigi wants that number on the record: FIFTEEN MINUTES from 'let's fix reality' to 'reality is in three pieces and Waluigi is in a fairy dimension surrounded by sentient mushrooms asking him riddles.' The Planar Fracture was not Waluigi's fault. It was the Oracle's ritual, Archie's unstable magic, and everyone's collective decision to IGNORE Waluigi when he raised concerns. Waluigi SAID something. Waluigi raised his hand—his beautiful, well-manicured hand—and said 'Is anyone else concerned about this?' And people SHUSHED him. They SHUSHED Waluigi. The great Waluigi, who was RIGHT, was SHUSHED. And then reality broke. Waluigi hopes everyone learned a lesson but Waluigi knows they didn't.
description:
Waluigi is going to document this catastrophe in DETAIL because future generations need to understand what happens when you build a reality-altering ritual on a foundation of Archie Miser's magic and optimism.

## The Setup (Where Everything Was Already Wrong)

Raventree Manor was already a problem BEFORE anyone decided to fix it with magic. The building existed across multiple dimensional layers simultaneously—Material Plane, Shadowfell, Feywild, and something called the Deep Mirror that Waluigi still doesn't fully understand and doesn't WANT to understand. The manor's architecture was WRONG. Rooms that shouldn't connect did. Mirrors reflected things that weren't there. Shadows moved independently of their sources.

Waluigi had been saying the manor was dangerous since the FIRST time he saw it. Waluigi noticed the mirrors were wrong. Waluigi noticed the shadows fell at angles that didn't match light sources. Waluigi noticed that the building felt like it was WATCHING. Did anyone listen to Waluigi? Does anyone EVER listen to Waluigi? The answer is no. The answer has ALWAYS been no.

The Oracle—one of multiple Oracles, because apparently ONE mysterious guide wasn't confusing enough—proposed a synchronization ritual. The theory was sound, Waluigi supposes, if you squint at it and ignore all the red flags. Align the three overlapping dimensional layers. Smooth out the planar wrinkles. Stop the wraiths and mirror monsters and general architectural hostility. On PAPER, it probably looked reasonable.

The problem was the EXECUTION.

## The Ritual (Where Waluigi Was Ignored)

The synchronization rite required three things it didn't have:

1. **Coordinated participants** — The party was ARGUING before the ritual started. Multiple people had different ideas about positioning. Nobody agreed on timing.

2. **All required personnel present** — Several key positions in the geometric array were left EMPTY because people were missing, distracted, or refusing to participate.

3. **A stable magical foundation** — And here's where Waluigi needs to pause and SCREAM into the void.

The ritual used ARCHIE MISER'S magic as its primary power source.

ARCHIE. MISER.

The man who resolves diplomatic disputes with FIREBALLS. The man whose magical signature is about as stable as a house of cards in a hurricane during an earthquake on a boat. The man who cast a fireball inside a WOODEN AIRSHIP and acted surprised when people got upset. THAT was the foundation they built the reality-altering ritual on.

Waluigi SAID something. Waluigi specifically raised his hand and asked 'Is anyone else concerned about this?' And people SHUSHED him. They made the 'quiet down' gesture. They told Waluigi to stop being negative. They said everything would be fine.

Fifteen minutes later, reality shattered.

Waluigi would like an apology. Waluigi will not receive one. Waluigi is used to this.

## The Fracture (01:30-01:45, Because Waluigi Checked His Watch)

The ritual began at approximately 01:30 in the morning because apparently nobody considered that maybe reality-altering magic should be performed during BUSINESS HOURS when people are ALERT and have had COFFEE.

For the first few minutes, it seemed to work. The dimensional boundaries around the manor shimmered, flexed, and began to align. Waluigi could feel the planes settling into harmony. It felt like the world exhaling after holding its breath. There was a moment—brief, fragile, almost beautiful—where everything clicked into place.

Then Archie's contribution destabilized.

Because OF COURSE it did.

Waluigi doesn't know the technical magical explanation. What Waluigi KNOWS is that the feedback was instant and catastrophic. The alignment didn't slip gently out of sync—it SHATTERED. Like glass. Like ice on a pond when you step wrong. The dimensional boundaries that were supposed to harmonize instead broke apart, and Raventree Manor—already a nexus of overlapping realities—split into three separate planar fragments.

The room spun. Colors inverted. Sound became light and light became pressure and PRESSURE became a force that picked Waluigi up and threw him sideways through a crack in reality that shouldn't have existed.

Fifteen minutes. From 'this might work' to 'Waluigi is in the Feywild now.' WAH.

## Where Everyone Ended Up (The Cosmic Scatter)

**THE SHADOWFELL — Shadow Estate**

Archie and Bowser were cast into the Shadowfell shard. Waluigi learned about their experience afterward and found it fitting that Archie ended up in the ONE dimension where fire magic doesn't work properly. The Shadowfell's planar physics suppressed fire. Archie without fire is like Waluigi without his hat—technically functional but missing the thing that defines him.

The Shadow Estate was a monochrome version of Raventree Manor. Same architecture, same layout, but drained of color and warmth. Everything in shades of grey and black. The air pressed down like the dimension itself was trying to flatten you into a shadow.

The estate was controlled by the Onyx Hand and their vampire lords—the Corvinarus family's undead branch. Centuries of political intrigue compressed into one haunted manor. The vampires viewed living visitors as either intrusions to punish or diversions to enjoy, and their idea of 'enjoyment' involved forced dinner parties where guests voted on who would die.

**THE FEYWILD — Overgrown Manor**

Waluigi ended up HERE. With Toad Lee. In the FEYWILD.

The Feywild version of Raventree Manor had been consumed by nature in the way nature consumes things when given unlimited time and zero supervision. Walls cracked open by root systems. Corridors choked with flowering vines that MOVED when you weren't looking directly at them. Rooms that had become self-contained ecosystems hosting giant insects, bioluminescent fungi, and fairy creatures who spoke in riddles and got OFFENDED if you solved them too quickly OR too slowly.

The Overgrown Manor was ruled by Lady Aurelian Corvinarus—the fey counterpart to the Shadowfell's vampire lords. Same family, different dimensional branch. Where the Shadowfell operated through undead hierarchy and blood politics, Lady Aurelian ran her court through fey logic. Obligations. Favors. Riddles. Social debts that multiplied if you acknowledged them and TRIPLED if you didn't.

Waluigi spent what felt like DAYS navigating social dynamics that changed based on the time of day, the phase of the moon, and apparently the ambient mood of local butterfly populations. Fey court politics made Mushroom Kingdom diplomacy look STRAIGHTFORWARD.

At least with spiders, you know where you stand. You're standing in a web and the spider wants to eat you. SIMPLE. With fey, you're standing in a conversation and the fairy wants you to owe them something, but they won't tell you WHAT or WHEN, and asking creates ANOTHER obligation.

Toad Lee was surprisingly good company for this ordeal. Quiet. Observant. Didn't trigger accidental fairy obligations by making eye contact with the wrong flower.

**THE DEEP MIRROR — Fractured Atrium**

Markop, Remi, and the Oracle vanished into the Deep Mirror, which was the WORST of the three by a significant margin.

The Deep Mirror was a dimension of crystalline structures, gravity that changed direction without warning, and time that DECAYED. Not just moved differently—DECAYED. Like fruit left on a counter. Things aged visibly. Edges frayed. The dimension was consuming itself and wanted to take everything inside along for the ride.

Waluigi did NOT end up in the Deep Mirror and he is GRATEFUL. The Feywild was exhausting but at least it was ALIVE. The Deep Mirror was DYING, and dying dimensions are apparently not pleasant places to be trapped.

**THE PHYSICAL PLANE — Ritual Room**

The ritual room—the only piece of Raventree Manor that stayed in normal reality—was seized by the Iron Legion within HOURS. Because the Iron Legion has the tactical instincts of a vulture and the moral compass of a calculator.

They recognized the room as an anchor point connecting the three fractured dimensions and immediately secured it. They also sent Toadburt into the Feywild as a coerced operative, fitted with an Entropy Ring to ensure compliance.

Waluigi has strong feelings about strapping obedience collars on people and sending them into alien dimensions. Those feelings can be summarized as: the Iron Legion is AWFUL.

## The Aftermath (Still Ongoing)

The Planar Fracture became the defining catastrophe of everything that followed. Every subsequent battle, alliance, betrayal, and desperate scramble for survival happened in its shadow.

The party was separated across three hostile dimensions with no way to communicate, no way to coordinate, and no way to know if the others were even alive. Waluigi spent every moment in the Feywild wondering whether Archie was dead in the Shadowfell, whether Markop was lost in the Deep Mirror, whether anyone was coming to help or whether 'help' was a concept that had fractured along with reality.

The Iron Legion controlled the only stable anchor point. Because of COURSE they did.

And throughout all of it, Waluigi remembered that he had RAISED CONCERNS. He had ASKED if anyone else was worried. He had been SHUSHED.

Waluigi survived the Feywild. Waluigi survived the fairy courts and the giant insects and the sentient vegetation and Lady Aurelian's INTERMINABLE riddle games. Waluigi survived because Waluigi is TOO STUBBORN to be destroyed by a dimensional catastrophe caused by people who didn't listen to him.

The universe has tried to break Waluigi many times. It has NEVER succeeded.

WAH.

## Lessons Learned (That Nobody Will Remember)

1. **Listen to Waluigi when he raises concerns.** This should be obvious but apparently requires stating explicitly.

2. **Do not build reality-altering rituals on Archie Miser's magic.** His magic is unstable. Everyone knows this. USE SOMEONE ELSE.

3. **Perform important rituals during business hours.** 01:30 AM is not a time for delicate magical work. It's a time for SLEEPING.

4. **Have backup plans for dimensional scatter.** Communication devices that work across planes. Meeting points. SOMETHING.

5. **The Iron Legion will exploit any opportunity.** Plan accordingly.

Waluigi does not expect anyone to remember these lessons. Waluigi has been giving good advice his entire life and watching people ignore it. But Waluigi is putting this on RECORD so that when everything goes wrong AGAIN, Waluigi can point here and say 'WALUIGI TOLD YOU.'

Because Waluigi DID tell them. And they shushed him.

They SHUSHED him.

Waluigi will NEVER forgive the shushing.

name: The Stone Auction
title: The Day Remi Was Sold for Twelve Thousand Gold (And Waluigi Was Not Even Surprised)
location: Raventree Manor — The Interior Gallery, The Library, The Auction Room
type: Supernatural Incident / Commercial Atrocity / Dimensional Humiliation
status: Resolved — Remi freed; Mystic Morel unresolved; Waluigi's nerves: unresolved
summary: Remi was turned to STONE by a Medusa. Then she was PUT IN AN ART SHOW. Then she was AUCTIONED OFF to the highest bidder. The winning bid was twelve thousand gold, placed by a man in a purple T who called himself Mystic Morel and who Waluigi immediately identified as a PROBLEM. Wario showed up, which he ALWAYS does, and a mages guild operative also appeared demanding Remi for THEMSELVES. Bowser threatened to burn everything down, which was the first sensible suggestion of the day. Markop broke a window. Remi was freed and immediately ran into Dan's arms. And the person responsible for the petrification — the Medusa, who put on a paper bag and walked through a wall like that was NORMAL — was never held accountable. Waluigi is keeping count. The number of people who have escaped consequences in this crisis is ASTRONOMICAL and growing.
description:
Waluigi is going to document this event in full because it represents a new category of catastrophe — not dimensional collapse, not architectural malice, not ritual failure — but the specific horror of watching a party member get turned into ART and then SOLD.

## The Medusa (Who Nobody Thought to Mention Was There)

Raventree Manor has a Medusa. This information was not in any briefing Waluigi received. Nobody said 'by the way, there is a creature living in this building whose PRIMARY ABILITY is turning people to stone.' Nobody left a NOTE. The warnings Waluigi found previously said 'don't clean the mirrors.' They did NOT say 'don't make eye contact with the resident Gorgon.' Waluigi considers this a significant gap in the available documentation.

The Medusa — a person, technically, a being with a face and clothing and apparently a SCHEDULE — turned Remi to stone with a glare. One glare. That was all it took. Remi made eye contact, the Medusa said something approximately translatable as 'smile,' and Remi became a statue. Remi, who has survived things that would have broken seasoned adventurers, who has walked through chaos with a cheerfulness that Waluigi finds simultaneously admirable and EXHAUSTING, was reduced to decorative stonework in SECONDS.

Then the Medusa put on a paper bag. Over her face. As if this were a reasonable and normal thing to do. And she walked into another room. Waluigi watched this happen. Waluigi has no explanation for the paper bag. Waluigi has filed the paper bag under 'things about this building that will haunt him' alongside the mirror warnings and the servant uniforms with no servants inside them.

## The Library Discovery (Where the Imps Were)

Before the auction could be located, the party needed to navigate the library. The library contained imps — flying, scribing creatures who wrote down everything the party said and did, instantly and in real time. Every statement. Every expression of confusion. Every muttered complaint. Documented.

Waluigi finds the imps philosophically interesting and practically INFURIATING. On one hand, Waluigi APPRECIATES thorough documentation. Waluigi IS thorough documentation. Waluigi understands the value of a complete record. On the other hand, the imps were documenting for the ARCHIVIST — a vampire, presumably, who sat behind a one-way mirror and watched visitors with academic detachment — and their documentation was being used against the party in real time.

Markop also noticed a statue of Vivesna in the library. Vivesna, who Markop killed. Standing there as if to say: 'Hello. Did you think there would be no record?' The manor keeps records of EVERYTHING. Every death. Every deed. Every person turned to stone and auctioned.

## The Archivist (One-Way Mirror, Infinite Condescension)

The Archivist's room was locked. Eager attempted to pick the lock. The window swung open and the Archivist informed them — with what Waluigi can only describe as vampire SMUG — that one cannot see vampires in mirrors because mirrors don't show them. One-way glass. Eager fell to the floor.

The Archivist then handed the party a poster. An OFFICIAL POSTER. Printed and distributed. It read: 'Official Art Display feat. Archie Miser' — with an image of Remi, turned to stone, presented as an art piece titled after ARCHIE, who WAS NOT EVEN THERE.

Waluigi needs to pause and register his objections. Remi was turned to stone. Remi was classified as an art piece. The art piece was named after Archie, who had nothing to do with this situation, simply because Archie's name apparently means something in this building's social hierarchy. Remi, who was ACTUALLY THERE and is a REAL PERSON, was reduced to supporting cast in her own petrification. Waluigi finds this offensive on multiple levels and intends to remember it.

## The Auction (Twelve Thousand Gold)

The auction room was accessed through a window that Markop used as an observation point before the situation required direct intervention. Through the window, the party watched a bidding war in progress. Remi — Remi, who Waluigi has watched dodge danger with the cheerfulness of someone who doesn't fully process that danger is dangerous — stood at the front of the room as stone. Inert. Sold.

Purple T won. Twelve thousand gold. The winning bidder — who would later identify himself as Mystic Morel — stood up and with an authority that suggested he did this regularly, freed Remi from her stone state. Then announced that she 'belonged to him.'

Waluigi has strong feelings about the phrase 'she belongs to me' and those feelings can be summarized as: NO. Waluigi does not care what was bid. Waluigi does not care what auction rules say. People are not PROPERTY and the Raventree auction house — which is apparently a THING that EXISTS — can take its entire operating structure and throw it into the ocean.

## The Room Erupts (Bowser's Finest Moment)

Markop broke the window. This was the correct response. Waluigi endorses window-breaking as a valid tactical option when the alternative is watching a party member get claimed as a purchased item.

The chaos that followed was, in Waluigi's assessment, textbook Disaster Inc. Wario appeared — from WHERE, Waluigi does not know, Wario simply APPEARS in chaotic situations like a bad omen in mustache form — and shoulder-barged Markop to the floor. A mages guild operative materialized and claimed Remi for THEMSELVES. Bowser pulled out a device to call his son for backup, which is either terrifying or comforting depending on how you feel about Koopa reinforcements. Markop summoned a moonbeam. Mystic Morel jumped out a window.

Salam started picking flowers. Waluigi does not have context for this. Waluigi has CHOSEN not to pursue context for this.

Remi ran out and jumped into Dan's arms. The auction was over.

## The Aftermath (Mystic Morel, Persistent Problem)

Remi was free. Remi was also standing next to Mystic Morel, who had jumped out the window and apparently landed directly into the aftermath of the situation he caused, which Waluigi considers AUDACIOUS.

Mystic Morel — Purple T, winning bidder, self-described owner of a person — explained himself with what the toads assessed as a LIE. He then offered tea. He offered incense. He insisted on following Remi 'to keep his end of the deal,' a deal that Remi had no memory of making, which is the most concerning detail of an extremely concerning afternoon.

A deal. With someone Remi doesn't remember. For a price she can't recall. Mystic Morel insists it exists. Remi cannot confirm or deny it. Waluigi has placed Mystic Morel in the category of 'problems that are currently walking around behind the party and have not been resolved.' That category is unfortunately crowded.

Wario also reappeared with a debt list the length of the mansion. Bowser owes him money. The list was long enough to cross a single item off and still remain longer than most legal documents Waluigi has encountered. Wario claimed the bomb he once gave Remi in a box was 'incidental.' Waluigi does not believe anything involving Wario is incidental. Wario is the OPPOSITE of incidental. Wario is purpose made.

title: How the Party Found a Broken Mirror in a Ghost's Bedroom, Mended It with the Youngest Member's Magic, Nearly Lost It to Wario, Discovered Every Enemy in the Building Gathered Around the Portal Circle, and Escaped Off the Roof Using a Feather While Servants Sang About Being Short and Stout

summary: I am documenting this session because it produced the third of four portal artifacts, introduced a sheep with an axe to the party roster, revealed that every major antagonist in the Shadow Estate has converged on the portal circle in the master bedroom, and ended with me watching Remi use a feather to float off a roof while servants below sang about being short and stout. The Mirror of True Reflection was found broken in Usk's private chambers, which is the ghost butler's bedroom and which contained two mundane mirrors on the floor, a ghost who yelled at us for touching his stuff, and the information that the mirror had been broken a while ago and possibly thrown out with the garbage. Remi mended it with a spell she apparently knows, which nobody had thought to ask her about because nobody asks Remi what she can do until the moment arrives when what she can do is the only thing that matters. Wario immediately tried to steal it. Markop stopped him by tripping him. The party now holds the black crystal, the orb of shadow domination, the umbral signet, and the Mirror of True Reflection. All four artifacts. The Midnight Fountain can be reactivated. Remi can go home. The path is open. The path is also currently blocked by a Medusa, a Beastmaster, hostile ghosts, singing servants, and the fact that the portal circle downstairs has become a convention center for every entity that wants to use the party or prevent the party from using it. WAH.
description:
I am documenting this session from the Feywild, where I have been since the Planar Fracture deposited me into Lady Aurelian's court alongside Hjumpik and Toad Lee. I was not present for any of the events described in this entry. I was reading a book in a dark room while following a dwarf by the sound of his footsteps when the events on the Shadow Estate's rooftop were occurring. I was arguing about whether to wing it on a balcony when Remi was floating off a roof holding a feather. I was healing Mystic Morel against my better judgment while Markop was landing on a person after jumping off a building.

Everything in this entry has been reconstructed from Markop's tactical debriefs, which are precise and emotionally honest in ways that read as painful to produce. From Remi's notes, which contain three exclamation points about the trampoline she did not land on and zero exclamation points about the Medusa who wanted to stuff her into taxidermy. From Green T's operational disclosures, which arrive in the specific format of someone who tells you exactly what you need to know and nothing else and leaves you to determine whether the nothing else is empty or full. From the toads' singing, which I have transcribed from Eager's memory because Eager remembers songs with the fidelity of someone who has been listening to them against his will for long enough that they have become permanent fixtures of his auditory architecture. And from Wario's account, which consists of Wario saying he smelled money and then everything else being inferred from what was missing from the room afterward.

I was not there. I document what I was not there for with the same rigor I apply to what I witness directly, because the record does not care about my location. The record cares about accuracy. My location is the Feywild. The accuracy is as close to complete as secondhand sourcing permits.

## Wario Picks a Lock and Smells Money

The session began with Wario picking a lock silently. I want to document the word silently because Wario's relationship with silence is approximately as reliable as Archie's relationship with fire safety, which is to say it exists in theory and collapses under observation. But in this instance Wario picked the lock without producing noise, which means either the lock was well-oiled, Wario has developed a technique for silent entry that he has not disclosed, or Wario's greed produces a focus so intense that it temporarily suppresses all other outputs including sound. I suspect the third option because I have known Wario long enough to watch his entire personality narrow to a single point of concentration when gold is nearby, and the narrowing produces a version of Wario that is more competent, more precise, and more dangerous than the version that operates when gold is not at stake.

Markop asked what Wario saw. Wario said he smelled money. He walked into the room. I want to note that Wario did not say he saw money. He said he smelled it. Wario's gold-sense, which I documented in the birthday session when his eyes turned gold in proximity to servant-pillow treasure, operates through multiple sensory channels. He sees gold through walls. He smells gold through doors. The sense is not metaphorical. It is a functional detection capability that the Mages Guild has not catalogued because the Mages Guild does not consider Wario a subject of magical study, which is an intelligence failure on their part that I find satisfying in a petty way because the Guild's blind spots are always about the people they consider beneath investigation.

Green T said he did not actually know where the mirror was. This admission, delivered with the casual directness of someone who has been pretending to have a plan and has decided that the pretense is no longer serving its purpose, recalibrated the party's expectations. Green T had been operating as though he knew where the artifacts were. He did not. He was navigating by instinct, reputation, and the accumulated intelligence of someone who has been inside the Shadow Estate longer than anyone else in the party. His instincts had produced results. The black crystal was on Vostolas's body. The shadow crystal came from the Beastmaster. But the mirror's location was a genuine unknown, and Green T's willingness to admit this rather than continue performing omniscience is, in my assessment, a sign of operational maturity that I respect even from across a dimensional boundary.

Markop said they still had not checked the main room where the purple toad had been. Remi said to check the door in front of them first. They agreed. Markop said it was okay to talk.

The toads started singing.

Markop said: as soon as I say it is okay to talk, you sing.

I am documenting this exchange because it is the most compressed possible representation of the Toad contingent's relationship with operational silence. They were told it was okay to talk. They interpreted okay to talk as okay to sing. The distinction between talking and singing is apparently nonexistent in Toad operational doctrine. Sound is sound. If sound is permitted, the sound they choose is musical. Markop's frustration was immediate and genuine and entirely futile because the toads have been singing at inappropriate moments since the beginning of the campaign and no amount of frustration has ever produced a behavioral change. They sing because they are toads and toads sing and the universe has not yet produced a consequence severe enough to make them stop.

The song, as transcribed from Eager's reluctant memory:

---

Creep and Crawl
(Performed by the Toads, unsanctioned, in the upper corridors of the Shadow Estate, immediately after being told it was okay to talk)

Creep and crawl, the Toads sneak through the halls,
Silent as the shadows on the walls!
Creep and crawl, we answer duty's calls,
Nothing's gonna stop us, nothing stalls!

Through the dark we tiptoe, soft and light,
Every door a mystery, every room a fright!
But we are the Toads who broke the glass,
And we will kick their — never mind, we'll pass!

Creep and crawl, with mirrors on the floor,
Ghosts are yelling at us, what's the score?
Creep and crawl, we're looking for the door,
Markop said be quiet — we sang more!

Wario smells the gold, Green T lost the plot,
Remi's got the mending spell that no one thought she got!
Rattles shakes his bones beside the crew,
Creep and crawl, the Toads are coming through!

Creep and crawl, the Toads sneak through the halls,
Louder than the silence, proud and tall!
Creep and crawl, until the curtain falls,
We're the Toads who sing through manor walls!

---

I am documenting this song in full because it was performed during what was supposed to be a covert approach to an unknown room in a hostile vampire estate, and because the song's lyrics include real-time operational intelligence about Wario smelling gold, Green T not knowing where the mirror was, Remi having a mending spell, and Rattles being present, all of which constitute the kind of information that an eavesdropping enemy could use to prepare countermeasures. The toads are not merely singing. They are broadcasting the party's capabilities, composition, and current objectives in verse form to anyone within earshot. This is either the worst possible operational security or the most effective psychological warfare available to a group whose primary weapon is the enemy's inability to take them seriously. I suspect both.

## Usk's Chambers: The Ghost, the Broken Mirror, and the Garbage

They entered Usk's private chambers. The room was more humbly appointed than the family rooms below but significantly larger than other servant quarters, which tells you something about Usk's position in the household hierarchy: important enough for space, not important enough for luxury. The furniture was plush with a seating area for guests, but both the sitting table and the writing desk were perpetually covered in papers and books in a state of disarray that Usk's otherwise meticulous personal presentation could not contain. Usk was organized in his person and disorganized in his management of other people's affairs, which is the specific contradiction of someone whose precision is self-directed rather than system-directed and who produces chaos in exactly the spaces where other people's lives intersect with his.

Ghosts were in the room. Not quiet ghosts. Commanding ghosts. Flying, haunting, declaring that they would haunt the Corvinarus family for generations. A big ghost demanded more slop while his ghost wife ordered servants to feed him. He burped ghostly remnant onto the floor. The domestic scene of an afterlife couple maintaining their living habits through death is the kind of detail that makes the Shadowfell simultaneously horrifying and banal, and I find the combination more unsettling than either quality alone because pure horror can be resisted and pure banality can be ignored but the two together produce a state of normalized dread that erodes your ability to tell which parts of your environment are dangerous and which are merely depressing.

Wario stole from the dresser while the party discussed who should look in the drawers. This is Wario operating at peak efficiency: the discussion about who should search is the distraction, and Wario uses the distraction to search first and take what he finds before the discussion concludes. By the time the party decided who should look, Wario had already looked and taken. The decision was made. It was made by Wario. It was made while everyone else was talking about making it.

Remi looked in a drawer. It was ransacked. Markop examined something inside. A powdery substance he could not identify. I am filing the powdery substance as unresolved intelligence because powdery substances in vampire estate servant quarters could be anything from alchemical components to narcotic residue to the kind of dust that accumulates in drawers that have not been opened since before the Planar Fracture, and the distinction matters but cannot be made from available sourcing.

Markop spotted two mundane mirrors on the floor. Green T inspected them. One had the right base. The base was correct for the Mirror of True Reflection. The mirror portion was not attached.

A ghost appeared. What are you doing with my stuff, the ghost demanded.

Markop asked: do you know what happened with this mirror? He showed the ghost the base.

The ghost said: oh, that. We broke it a while ago. Maybe we threw it out. We used it to see each other.

I need to document what we used it to see each other means because the phrasing is doing significant work. The Mirror of True Reflection shows true forms rather than appearances. In a dimension where imps wear Wario costumes and tanukis wear Toadburt faces and Vivian wore Vivesna's identity for weeks, a mirror that shows true forms is the single most valuable intelligence tool available. It strips performances. It removes disguises. It shows what is rather than what is presented.

Usk and whoever the we refers to used this mirror to see each other. Not to check their hair. Not to examine their appearance. To see each other. In a building where everyone is performing a version of themselves that serves institutional purposes, two entities used the Mirror of True Reflection to bypass those performances and look at each other as they actually were. This is either the most romantic or the most operationally paranoid use of a planar artifact that I have ever documented, and the two possibilities are not mutually exclusive. I suspect both were true simultaneously, because in the Shadowfell, love and paranoia operate on the same frequency: the desperate need to know that the person beside you is real.

The mirror was broken. The mirror was possibly thrown out with the garbage. Markop looked out the window. Garbage was piled up below.

Markop asked: can we just remake it?

The ghost's response was delivered at a volume and with an intensity that Markop's account preserves with the specific fidelity of someone who was standing close enough to feel the temperature drop:

I DONT KNOW CAN YOU OPEN PLANAR FRACTURES ON A WHIM? ARE YOU MAGICALLY ATTUNED TO THINGS? I DONT THINK SO THIS IS HORRIBLE!

The ghost was upset. Not about property damage. About the loss of the only tool that allowed honest perception in a dimension built on dishonest presentation. The screaming was grief disguised as anger, which is the most common form of grief in institutional environments where expressing grief directly would be read as weakness. The ghost screamed because the mirror was how the ghost saw someone, and the mirror was broken, and broken things in the Shadowfell stay broken because the Shadowfell specializes in permanence of damage.

I find the ghost's outburst one of the most emotionally honest moments in the entire Shadeward arc. It was directed at a centaur who was asking a practical question about artifact repair, and the answer was not practical at all. The answer was: I have lost the ability to see someone honestly and you are asking me about glue.

## The Roof: Searching the Garbage and Finding the Piece

They searched the roof. Markop found a book called The Wario Method and fifteen gold. I am filing The Wario Method without comment except to note that any book titled after Wario's methodology that is found on a roof near discarded garbage has either been studied and discarded or deliberately planted, and I cannot determine which without reading it, and I do not currently have access to it from the Feywild, and I am not certain I want access to a book that codifies Wario's approach to anything.

Remi found a shiny piece of glass.

Green T said: that is a part of the mirror. Give it to me.

Remi said okay. She gave it to Green T.

Green T said: now Markop, give me the base.

Markop thought about this. He assessed the artifact distribution. He had the orb of shadow domination and the black crystal. Remi had the umbral signet. If Green T got the mirror, the distribution would be three people holding four artifacts. No single person controlling the exit. Green T's request for both parts of the mirror, the piece from Remi and the base from Markop, positioned him as the artifact's custodian, which is a role Green T has been positioning himself for throughout the Shadeward arc. Green T understands that holding artifacts is holding leverage, and leverage is how former crime lords maintain relevance in groups that did not invite them.

Markop gave the base to Green T. The distribution was accepted as fair.

Green T looked around. He did not have anything to repair the mirror. The piece and the base were separate. A broken Mirror of True Reflection is two objects, not one, and two objects do not show true forms. He asked if anyone had a mending spell.

One person spoke up. A gruff voice. Merric, the axe-wielding sheep from earlier sessions who had been operating on the periphery of the party's awareness without being formally recruited.

Remi interrupted him.

I know a mending spell, she said.

They all looked at her.

I need to document this moment with the attention it deserves because it is the moment where Remi's capabilities exceeded the party's expectations of her for the first time in a way that did not involve violence or being tricked.

Remi knows Mending. Nobody asked. Nobody checked. Nobody said hey Remi, do you have any utility spells that might be useful for repairing planar artifacts that we need to escape a death dimension. The party has been carrying Remi through the Shadowfell as a combination of liability and combat asset, tracking her trust failures and her kneecap shots and her shadow blade executions and her tendency to accept gifts from people who are trying to enthrall her. Nobody tracked her spell list. Nobody asked what else she could do besides fight and be targeted.

She also said: Thunderclap also sounds scary, and scariness comes in handy.

She began to clap. Thunder cla—

Someone stopped her before she could finish the clap, which I am documenting as evidence that the party has learned, through painful experience, that Remi's enthusiasm for demonstrating her capabilities does not include a filter for whether the demonstration is appropriate to the current tactical environment. A thunderclap in the upper floor of a vampire estate while the party is trying to avoid detection would have produced the same result as the toad singing: every hostile entity in the building converging on their position. Someone physically prevented Remi from completing the gesture, which means someone was close enough to Remi to grab her hands mid-clap, which means someone in the party has developed the specific reflex of monitoring Remi's hand movements for imminent loud magic. I find this development both necessary and sad.

Remi got the mirror pieces. She cast Mending. The broken piece and the base reconnected. The Mirror of True Reflection was whole again.

Remi said: well, it has been a while since I looked at myself in a mirror. I am probably dirty, but I will give it back to Green T.

I am sitting with this line from across a dimensional boundary because it contains something I did not expect from Remi and which I find significant enough to document with full attention even though I was not there to hear it said.

Remi looked at herself in the Mirror of True Reflection. The mirror that shows true forms. The mirror that strips performances and reveals what is underneath. The mirror that Usk used to see someone honestly in a dimension built on dishonest presentation. Remi looked into it and her response was: I am probably dirty.

She was not alarmed. She was not transformed. She was not confronted by a version of herself that she did not recognize. She looked at her true form and saw someone who needed a bath. This means either the Mirror of True Reflection shows Remi as Remi because Remi IS her true form and there is no performance to strip, or the mirror showed Remi something she has already accepted about herself and the acceptance prevented the shock that the mirror is designed to produce.

I find the first possibility more likely and more important. Remi does not perform. This is the thing I have been documenting across multiple entries from the Feywild without stating it this directly: Remi's vulnerability to the Shadow Estate's deceptions is not because she is performing trust and the performance can be manipulated. It is because she IS trusting and the trust is genuine and genuine things cannot be stripped by a mirror because there is nothing between the surface and the truth. The Mirror of True Reflection cannot shock someone who has no gap between their presented self and their actual self. Remi looked into the mirror and saw Remi. Dirty, tired, battle-scarred, purple-eyed Remi. No revelation. No hidden layer. Just her.

This is why the Shadow Estate keeps trying to add layers to her. The friendship rings, the enthrallment contracts, the invisible tightening ring, the birthday cake. They are not stripping Remi's defenses. They are trying to BUILD defenses onto someone who does not have them, because a person without defenses cannot be controlled through their defenses and must instead be controlled through additions. You cannot manipulate what is not there. You can only add something new and then manipulate that.

Remi gave the mirror back to Green T. She said she would give it back. She did. This is also Remi: she says things and then she does them. The gap between statement and action that the Shadow Estate exploits in everyone else does not exist in Remi because Remi does not maintain a gap.

Markop examined the mirror for magic. He noticed magic. He was reaching for it.

Swipe.

Wario swiped the mirror. Markop dragged Wario. Pulled him. Wario tripped.

Hey, you tricked us, Markop said.

Wario said: I never said you can keep the mirror. I only said I can have it.

I am documenting this exchange from the Feywild with the specific appreciation of someone who has been Wario's business partner for decades and who recognizes this maneuver as the foundational technique of Wario's entire operating philosophy. Wario did not lie. He did not say the party could keep the mirror. He said he wanted the mirror. The party assumed that wanting the mirror and accepting the party's claim to the mirror were the same thing. They are not. Wario's ethics operate on the specific distinction between what he says and what others infer from what he says, and the gap between those two things is where Wario lives and where Wario's profits accumulate. I have been on both sides of this gap. I have profited from it and I have been robbed by it. The gap is real. The gap is Wario.

Markop negotiated. If Wario helped them get the remaining items and kill the Scarecrow, Wario could have the mirror afterward. Wario agreed. I will loot its body though, he added.

This is the deal. Wario gets the Mirror of True Reflection after the campaign objectives are completed. Wario also gets the Scarecrow's loot. The party gets Wario's assistance for the remaining operations. The economics are Wario's economics: nothing is free, everything has a price, and the price should be paid to Wario. I respect the consistency even while finding it exhausting from across a dimensional boundary.

## The Thud: What Remi Saw Below

A thud came from the floor below. Someone spoke. A sound was heard.

Remi used a rope to descend and investigate. Markop held the rope. Remi went down.

She saw people entering the master bedroom. The master bedroom that dominates the estate's upper floor. Red furnishings. Silver vases with blood-petal roses. Velvet curtains half-drawn. The desk for two. The view of bleak dark lands.

Tanukiburt was there. The real Toadburt was there, injured. They were surrounding the planar portal circle, covering and uncovering it from a rug. Mystic Morel was there.

I need to document what this tableau means from the Feywild because it changes the operational landscape in ways that affect both dimensional fragments simultaneously.

Every significant antagonist in the Shadow Estate has converged on the portal circle. The tanuki who impersonated Toadburt at the birthday trap. The real Toadburt who has been injured and whose whereabouts have been a mystery since Vostolas erased him from the records. Mystic Morel, the fortune teller who stole Archie's dimensional tools and placed an invisible ring on Remi and opened unauthorized portals and sang songs about destiny while emptying pockets.

They are all at the portal circle. They are all doing something with it. The covering and uncovering of the rug suggests they are either activating the circle, testing the circle, modifying the circle, or preparing the circle for someone else's use. The rug is the layer between the circle and the room. Removing it exposes the circle. Replacing it conceals it. The oscillation between exposure and concealment implies either uncertainty about whether the circle should be active or a process that requires both states in sequence.

The portal circle is the party's exit. The portal circle is what the four artifacts activate. The portal circle is the mechanism that connects the Shadeward to the ruined manor and potentially to the Feyward and the material plane. And the entities gathered around it include a shapeshifter, a fortune teller with dimensional transit capabilities, and an injured toad whose presence implies either rescue or further exploitation.

The party has all four artifacts. The portal circle has all the party's enemies standing on top of it. These two facts produce the specific operational challenge of holding the key to the door while the door is being used as a conference table by the people who want to lock the door permanently. Or open it for their own purposes. Or do something with it that the party has not been briefed on because nobody briefs Disaster Inc. on anything until the briefing's content is already trying to kill them.

Remi lost focus. She slipped on the rope. She tumbled into a bush outside the window.

Lyranth the Sculptor and Vaxillus Loumaal were there. The Medusa and the Beastmaster. Together. Outside the window that Remi had just fallen through.

Vaxillus saw Remi. Waved. The wave was the specific social gesture of someone who considers the person they are waving at to be a future acquisition rather than a current threat.

They sorted their distance. They positioned themselves far enough away that Lyranth's petrification gaze would not accidentally activate on Remi before they wanted it to.

We do not want to turn them to stone, someone said. We now like to stuff them into taxidermy.

I am documenting this sentence from the Feywild with the full weight it deserves because it represents an evolution in the Beastmaster's collection methodology that I find significant. Previously, Lyranth turned things to stone and Vaxillus collected things as taxidermy. These were separate operations serving separate aesthetic goals. Now the operations have merged. They do not want to petrify. They want to stuff. The collection has expanded from statues to specimens. Remi is not being targeted for a display case. She is being targeted for the kind of preservation that involves removing the interior and replacing it with cotton and wire and the specific craft sensibility of someone who knits rugs from the pelts of Shadowfell apex predators and names his crossbows Blood Spiller and Heart Killer.

Green T called from above: come join us.

Markop threw another ladder as they cut the original one. Remi started running up. Vaxillus overtook her. Markop stepped on Vaxillus's hands as Remi climbed on the Beastmaster's back. Remi jumped onto Vaxillus's back and climbed up using the Beastmaster as a biological ladder.

Another rope hit a guard's head below. HEY, BE CAREFUL WITH THAT THING, the guard yelled. I am documenting the guard's complaint because it is the most procedurally normal response to anything that happened during this session and because procedural normality from a guard in a vampire estate during a rooftop pursuit is its own kind of surrealism that I appreciate from the relative safety of the Feywild.

Vaxillus grabbed Lyranth. They got on a second-story windowsill and went inside, running upstairs. They were coming.

Remi was up safely.

## Merric the Sheep Joins the Party

The sheep said: let us go, team.

Markop said: wait, who even are you?

Merric said: what do you mean? I am part of the team.

Markop said: what is my name then?

Merric said: Centerus.

Markop said: wrong.

Merric said: wait, I know this one.

Markop said: why do you not join our team instead?

Merric thought about it. Said: sure, why not.

The party is now larger. An axe-wielding sheep who cannot correctly identify the party leader by name has been formally recruited through a process that took approximately fifteen seconds and involved zero vetting, zero background checks, and zero consideration of whether an axe-wielding sheep might have ulterior motives for wanting to join a group that is carrying four planar artifacts while being pursued by a Medusa and a Beastmaster.

This is how Disaster Inc. recruits. The standard is: do you exist? Are you here? Can you hold something? Welcome aboard. I have been documenting this recruitment pattern from the Feywild throughout the campaign and it has not changed once. Rattles the skeleton was recruited in similarly expedited fashion. The tanuki was briefly a party member before being exposed. Green T was recruited through demonstrated usefulness during surreal emergencies. The party's recruitment policy is not selective. It is reactive. You join by being present when the party needs someone present, and the vetting happens after, if it happens at all.

Merric had been distracting Lyranth and Vaxillus long enough for the party to operate on the upper floor. A Koopa was seen exiting a window to the right during the standoff, and Merric smirked, suggesting the distraction had been coordinated. Whether Merric and the Koopa are working together, whether the Koopa is the same Koopa from the Star Shard Caves who used the unstable teleporter, and whether either of them has an agenda beyond immediate survival, I cannot determine from the Feywild. I am filing both.

## The Rooftop Trap: Doors Locked, Arrows Aimed, Servants Singing

The door slammed open as they tried to exit the roof. Lyranth the Sculptor and Vaxillus Loumaal were there. Ghosts that had been complaining about their stuff in Usk's chambers were now hostile. The guard from below was working with them.

We have you surrounded, someone said. All doors are locked. This will not be another archivist battle. You cannot sneak out the door now.

I am documenting the phrase this will not be another archivist battle from the Feywild because it reveals that the estate's remaining power structure has studied the Vostolas engagement and drawn operational conclusions from it. Vostolas attacked in a corridor. Vostolas was smited out of the air. Vostolas was kneecapped, tied up, and executed. The estate learned from that failure. They locked the doors first. They brought ranged support. They positioned ghosts for energy drain. They brought the Medusa and the Beastmaster together rather than deploying them separately. The current tactical setup was specifically designed to prevent the party from doing what they did to Vostolas: running, splitting, and counterattacking from unexpected angles.

All arrows and ghosts were aimed at the party. The rooftop was a kill box. The doors were locked. The ground was two stories down. The estate had learned.

Remi grabbed a feather.

Feather fall time, she said.

The skeleton Rattles, Remi, and three toads, Eager, Salam, and Dan, grabbed onto Remi. They descended softly. Feather Fall converts a lethal problem into a gentle one without requiring any modification of the environment or confrontation with the threat that produced the need to fall. You do not fight the rooftop trap. You leave the rooftop. The trap remains set. You are no longer in it.

Remi jumped off the roof. She saw a trampoline on the ground. She landed right next to it. Not on it. Next to it. The trampoline was there. Remi did not use the trampoline. Whether the trampoline was placed as an alternative escape mechanism, as bait, or as an unrelated piece of estate furniture, I cannot determine from the Feywild. But Remi landing next to a trampoline instead of on it is the most Remi possible outcome of a rooftop escape and I am documenting it because the record should contain the trampoline and Remi's relationship to it, which is adjacent.

Servants started surrounding Markop on the roof. Ghosts were draining him. He was getting tired. The ghosts pulled energy with the persistent, unhurried appetite of entities that feed on vitality and have all the time in the Shadowfell.

Servants popped up and began singing. The full song, as transcribed from multiple accounts that agree on the lyrics if not on the melody:

---

We Are the Servants
(Performed by the Shadow Estate's ghostly household staff during a rooftop military engagement, approximately 15th-16th Harvestide, 1040 BF)

We are the servants, short and stout,
Here is my ghostly, here is my spout!
When the master calls and the blood runs out,
We tip ourselves over and pour it out!

We are the servants, pale and thin,
We polish the silver, we sweep within!
When the guests are screaming and arrows sing,
We hum our tune and we do our thing!

We are the servants, cold and grey,
We served the manor in life's bright day!
Now we serve the manor in death's dim light,
And we'll keep on serving through every night!

Dust the shelves and mop the floor,
Guests are jumping, what's that for?
Feathers falling, toads descending,
Service never, ever ending!

We are the servants, short and stout,
We do not know what the fuss is about!
The doors are locked, the ghosts are fed,
And we'll be here long after you are dead!

---

I am documenting this song from the Feywild because it is the most precisely Shadowfell artifact of the entire session. The servants are not combatants. They are not allies. They are not enemies. They are the institutional backdrop. The people who maintained the building in life and maintain it in death. When violence erupts above them, they respond not with flight or fight but with SONG. They sing because singing is what servants do when they cannot control what is happening around them. The song is not tactical. The song is coping. And the coping sounds like a nursery rhyme about teapots adapted for ghostly household staff who have been performing domestic service for so long that death did not interrupt their routine, merely changed the lighting.

The line we do not know what the fuss is about is the most devastating line in the song because it is probably true. The servants genuinely may not understand why the living are jumping off roofs. The servants have been dead for an unspecified duration. They continue working. They continue singing. The concept of urgency has been replaced by the concept of schedule. There is no fuss. There is only service. The service continues. The service has always continued. The service will continue after everyone currently alive in the building has stopped being alive, and the servants will sweep up afterward and hum while they do it.

Wario tugged on Markop. We need to get out of here, Wario said.

Markop dashed. Dodged ghosts. Jumped off the roof. He did not land on the trampoline. He landed on a person instead. The person said oof. Markop said nothing because Markop was already running.

He saw Remi and the others running away downward along the bone-white paths of paving stones hemmed in by fine gray brickwork, the walkways spotless and pristine except for a sprinkling of faded crimson petals and stiff stony gray leaves from the surrounding flora. He followed them.

The party was running. Again. Through the Shadow Estate's grounds. Again. With hostile entities behind them. Again. Carrying artifacts that could reshape dimensional connections. Again.

This is the operational rhythm of the Shadeward campaign as I have documented it from the Feywild through every account and artifact and fragment that has reached me across the dimensional boundary. Acquire something. Be pursued for acquiring it. Run. Regroup. Plan the next acquisition while bleeding from the previous one. The rhythm has not changed since the dinner party. The scale has. The dinner party involved one vampire lord and one children's table sniper. The current pursuit involves a Medusa, a Beastmaster, hostile ghosts, singing servants, a locked rooftop, and every significant antagonist in the building gathered around the one exit that matters.

## What the Party Now Holds

I am documenting the current artifact distribution from the Feywild because it matters enormously and because the party achieved it through a combination of execution, diplomacy, theft, and mending that I find characteristic of Disaster Inc.'s operational methodology.

The Black Crystal: secured from Vostolas's body after Remi executed him with a shadow blade. Obtained through violence that followed from betrayal that followed from a birthday trap.

The Orb of Shadow Domination: secured from Vaxillus the Beastmaster through negotiated exchange. Obtained through diplomacy conducted from an information disadvantage.

The Umbral Signet: in Remi's possession. The youngest and most frequently targeted member of the party carrying a planar authority seal through a dimension full of entities who want to use it.

The Mirror of True Reflection: recovered from Usk's chambers as a broken base and a piece of glass found on the roof. Mended by Remi using a spell nobody knew she had. Nearly stolen by Wario. Currently held by Green T under an agreement that Wario gets it after the Scarecrow is defeated.

Four artifacts. Four holders. One portal circle. The circle is in the master bedroom. The master bedroom currently contains Tanukiburt, the real Toadburt, and Mystic Morel.

The party has the keys. The enemies are standing on the lock.

## The Path Forward

The party is running through the Shadow Estate's grounds with all four artifacts needed to reactivate the Midnight Fountain. Behind them are Lyranth the Sculptor, Vaxillus Loumaal, hostile ghosts, and the institutional apparatus of a vampire estate that has been studying their methods and adapting its responses. In front of them is the portal circle, currently occupied by antagonists. Somewhere in the building, Mystic Morel is doing something with the circle that involves covering and uncovering it. Somewhere in the building, the real Toadburt is injured. Somewhere in the building, the tanuki is back.

Remi wants to go home. She said so on her birthday. She has been saying it since she arrived. The artifacts are in the party's hands. The path is technically open.

The path is also full of people standing on it.

This is the Shadowfell's final lesson, the one it has been teaching since the cold awakening when Archie lost his fire: having what you need is not the same as being able to use what you need. You can hold the key and still be locked in. You can see the door and still be trapped. The dimension does not deny you the tools. It denies you the conditions under which the tools function.

Thirty seconds. Four artifacts. One circle. A building full of entities whose interests range from enthrallment to taxidermy to fortune-telling to whatever the real Toadburt's presence implies about plans that have been running underneath the party's awareness since before they arrived.

The party runs downhill. The party always runs downhill. Disaster Inc. does not retreat upward. It retreats toward whatever is at the bottom, because the bottom is where the next problem lives and the party would rather face the next problem than remain in the current one.

I am in the Feywild. I cannot help them. I cannot run with them. I can document what they did and what they found and what they are carrying and what is chasing them. I can note that Remi mended a planar artifact with a spell nobody asked her about and that the mirror showed her nothing she did not already know about herself and that the toads sang during a covert approach and that the servants sang during a combat engagement and that Wario tried to steal the mirror and that Markop landed on a person and that a sheep was recruited in fifteen seconds.

I can note that the party has all four keys and the door is occupied.

I can note that Remi wants to go home.

I can note that from the Feywild, I cannot tell whether she will make it.

WAH.

waluigiAssessment:
Waluigi was not present for the Shadeward Arc. Waluigi was in the Feywild being physically dragged between rooms by a dwarf and a dragon-blooded aristocrat while a dryad commented that the scene reminded her of kindergarten. Waluigi has reconstructed the Shadeward Arc from Archie's account, Green T's account, Markop's account of finding artifacts that implied Archie's prior presence, and the deeply unsettling confirmation from multiple sources that Archie spent time working alongside the Purple Legion and an entity described variously as an aberration, a ghost, and something else depending on who is being asked.

Archie fought a deity. He escaped a vampire prison using empty quivers and self-deprecating theater. He lived alone in a death dimension for a month. He was drafted by the Mages Guild. He was robbed by a singing fortune teller who used his stolen tools to open a portal. He summoned a thundercloud and flew to the Tree of Woe.

Waluigi has criticized Archie extensively in this encyclopedia. The criticisms are accurate and documented and will remain. But Waluigi is also going to document this clearly and without qualification: the Shadeward Arc is the strongest evidence available that Archie Miser is more than the fireball he leads with. Strip the fire away and what remains is someone who survives. Someone who adapts. Someone who looked at a god's offer of everything and said no and walked toward the Shadowfell instead.

The fireball is what Archie does first. What he does after that is who he actually is.

Waluigi would appreciate it if nobody told Archie he wrote this.

WAH.
